title: Limits at infinity
goal: See what a function settles toward far to the right ($x \to +\infty$) or far to the left ($x \to -\infty$) by focusing on the biggest power in the top and bottom.

beforeThis.skill: Watch out for negative $x$: $\sqrt{x^2} = |x|$, which equals $+x$ when $x > 0$, but equals $-x$ when $x < 0$ (far to the left)!

seeIt.creator: Dr. Trefor Bazett
seeIt.watchFor: Shows $\lim_{x \to \infty} \arctan x = \pi/2$ as one horizontal asymptote.

seeIt.title: Limits at Infinity & Horizontal Asymptotes
seeIt.creator: Organic Chemistry Tutor
seeIt.watchFor: Divides by the highest power, including under a square root, to get the limit of a rational function as $x \to \pm\infty$.

questions.asking: Write down an example of a polynomial $f(x)$ that stays finite as $x \to \infty$ and as $x \to -\infty$.
questions.statement: Give a polynomial $f(x)$ with the property that both $\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x)$ and $\lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x)$ are (finite) real numbers.

questions.asking: Write down an example of a polynomial $f(x)$ whose behaviour as $x \to \infty$ is different from its behaviour as $x \to -\infty$.
questions.statement: Give a polynomial $f(x)$ that satisfies $\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) \ne \lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x)$.

questions.asking: Look at the highest-power term (the leading term) to see whether the polynomial shoots up to $+\infty$ or down to $-\infty$ when $x$ is huge and positive.
Factor the highest power of $x$ out of the square root and the denominator to see what horizontal height the fraction flattens out to as $x \to +\infty$.
Compare the highest power of $x$ in the top and bottom (or divide every term by that highest power) to see what number the fraction settles toward as $x \to -\infty$.
Divide the top and bottom by the highest power of $x$ to see what ratio the leading terms settle toward as $x \to +\infty$.
Focus on the highest power of $x$ in the numerator and denominator to find the horizontal asymptote as $x \to +\infty$.
Find the exact value of the limit as $x \to -\infty$, taking care with the signs of even and odd roots for negative $x$.
First find what the inside of the trig function approaches as $x \to -\infty$, then evaluate the trig function at that angle.
Pull $x^2$ out of the square root carefully—since $x \to -\infty$ is negative, remember that $\sqrt{x^2} = |x| = -x$!
Factor out the largest power of $x$ as $x \to -\infty$, watching the minus sign when pulling $x^2$ out of a square root ($\sqrt{x^2} = -x$ for $x < 0$).
Check if a single rational function can approach two different finite numbers at $+\infty$ and $-\infty$, or explain why no such rational function exists.
questions.statement: Give a rational function $f(x)$ with the properties that $\lim_{x \to \infty} f(x) \ne \lim_{x \to -\infty} f(x)$, and both limits are (finite) real numbers.

questions.asking: Interpret in real-world terms what it means if the concentration $c(t)$ in your body does not approach $0$ as time $t \to \infty$.
questions.statement: Suppose the concentration of a substance in your body $t$ hours after injection is given by some formula $c(t)$, and $\lim_{t \to \infty} c(t) \ne 0$. What kind of substance might have been injected?
